title: Hochschild homology and the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem
summary: Classical ungraded Hochschild homology and cohomology of an associative algebra over a commutative ring with bimodule coefficients, on Mathlib's homological-complex carriers: simplicial construction, normalisation over every k, low degrees and square-zero extensions, the bar resolution with Ext and Tor over the enveloping algebra, the cup product and its Yoneda comparison, an explicit sign dictionary with DGAInfinity Layer 8 giving Gerstenhaber's homotopy formula and graded commutativity, the antisymmetrisation of RefinedTraceMethods §1.9 on the classical complex, and the cohomological HKR theorem for smooth k-projective algebras over any commutative ring (canonical isomorphism T^• ≅ HH^• of graded algebras, determinant cocycle = n! times it), with the polynomial case computed unconditionally from the Koszul resolution.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.cohomologyTwoClassification
targets.statement: A k-split square-zero extension of A by M (k-algebra E, surjective algebra map p:E→A, injective k-linear i:M→E with range ker p, i(m)i(m')=0, e·i(m)=i(p(e)m), i(m)·e=i(m p(e)), admitting a k-linear section) is isomorphic over A and under M to A⊕_{f_s}M with f_s(a,a')=i⁻¹(s(a)s(a')−s(aa')) a cocycle; changing s changes f_s by a coboundary; A⊕_f M ≅ A⊕_{f'} M compatibly iff f−f' ∈ B²; the projection of A⊕_f M has an algebra section iff [f]=0. Hence HH²(A,M) is in bijection with isomorphism classes of k-split square-zero extensions inducing the given bimodule structure, 0 ↔ TrivSqZeroExt A M.

api.statement: Tor_0^{Aᵉ}(M,N) ≅ M ⊗_{Aᵉ} N naturally in N.

api.statement: Tor_n^{Aᵉ}(M,P)=0 for projective P and n≥1; Tor is computed by any projective resolution and is functorial in M.

api.statement: HH_n(A,M) ≅ Tor_n^{Aᵉ}(M,A) for k-projective A.

tests.name: tor_zero
tests.statement: Tor_0^{Aᵉ}(M,A) ≅ M/[A,M]; for A=M=Mat₂(k) it is k.

tests.name: tor_k
tests.statement: For A=k, Tor_0(M,k)=M and Tor_n(M,k)=0 for n≥1.

tests.name: tor_free
tests.statement: Tor_n^{Aᵉ}(M,Aᵉ)=0 for n≥1 and Tor_0 ≅ M.

tests.name: tor_wrong_side

targets.name: HochschildHKR.cup
targets.statement: The k-bilinear cup product C^p(A,A) × C^q(A,A) → C^{p+q}(A,A), (f∪g)(a₁,…,a_{p+q}) = f(a₁,…,a_p) g(a_{p+1},…,a_{p+q}).
hypotheses: k a commutative ring
A a ring with Algebra k A

api.name: HochschildHKR.cup_assoc
api.statement: ∪ is associative with unit 1 ∈ C⁰(A,A)=A.

api.name: HochschildHKR.cup_zero_left
api.statement: x∪g = (a↦x g(a)), f∪y=(a↦f(a)y); in degree (0,0) it is the multiplication of A.

api.name: HochschildHKR.cup_normalized
api.statement: Normalised cochains are closed under ∪; for commutative R, ∪ is R-bilinear and x∪g is the R-structure of 1.5.

tests.name: cup_unit
tests.statement: 1∪f=f=f∪1; the reversed-order product g(…)f(…) is associative (cup product of Aᵒᵖ) but breaks the Leibniz rule: for Mat₂(k), x=E₁₁, g=id, the defect at (E₂₁,E₁₂) is E₁₁−E₂₂.

tests.name: cup_square
tests.statement: For ∂ on k[x], (∂∪∂)(x,x)=1: a nonzero cochain whose class vanishes (6.2).

targets.name: HochschildHKR.cup_leibniz
targets.statement: δ(f∪g)=δf∪g+(−1)^p f∪δg for f∈C^p(A,A); hence HH^•(A,A)=⊕_n HH^n(A,A) is an associative unital graded k-algebra with degree-zero part Z(A), and a graded R-algebra for commutative R.
hypotheses: k a commutative ring
A a ring with Algebra k A

targets.name: HochschildHKR.extMk_comp_extMk
targets.statement: In an abelian category with enough projectives and HasExt, for projective resolutions P of X and Q of Y, cocycles f:P_p→Y and g:Q_q→Z, and a family f̃_i:P_{i+p}→Q_i with ε_Q∘f̃₀=f and d∘f̃_{i+1}=f̃_i∘d, Abelian.Ext.comp (P.extMk f) (Q.extMk g) = s(p,q)·P.extMk (f̃_q ≫ g) for a sign s(p,q)∈{±1} depending only on p and q, with s(p,0)=1.
hypotheses: C an abelian category with EnoughProjectives and HasExt
P a projective resolution of X, Q of Y
f, g cocycles of degrees p, q
f̃ a strictly commuting lift of f

targets.name: HochschildHKR.cohomologyIsoExt_cup
targets.statement: For A projective over k and cocycles f∈Z^p(A,A), g∈Z^q(A,A), θ_{p+q}[f∪g] = (−1)^{pq} s(p,q)·Abelian.Ext.comp (θ_p[f]) (θ_q[g]) with θ of 4.4 and s of 5.3; the strictly commuting lift f̃_i(a₀⊗a₁⊗…⊗a_{p+i+1}) = (−1)^{pi} a₀ f(a₁,…,a_p)⊗a_{p+1}⊗…⊗a_{p+i+1} composed with g is (−1)^{pq} f∪g.
hypotheses: k a commutative ring
A a ring with Algebra k A
Module.Projective k A

layers.title: Comparison with the graded and derived carriers

targets.name: HochschildHKR.suspendCochain_coboundary
targets.statement: For A in degree zero, 𝒜 = TauCeti.IsNonUnitalDGAlgebra.toAInfinityAlgebra of the trivially graded A with zero differential: for n ≥ 1, Θ: C^n(A,A) → TauCeti.AInfinityAlgebra.PositiveHochschild.cochains 𝒜 (n−1), Θf∘s^{⊗n}=s∘f, is a k-linear isomorphism (degree n−1 cochains are exactly the arity-n ones), with, for p,q ≥ 1, Θ(δf)=(−1)^{p+1}·TauCeti.AInfinityAlgebra.hochschildDifferential 𝒜 (p−1) (Θf), Θ(f∘g)=TauCeti.ReducedTensorWords.brace (Θf) (Θg) (q−1) for the Gerstenhaber composition (f∘g)(a)=Σ_{i=1}^p(−1)^{(i−1)(q−1)} f(…,g(a_i,…,a_{i+q−1}),…), and Θ{f,g}=TauCeti.ReducedTensorWords.gerstenhaberBracket (p−1) (q−1) (Θf) (Θg) with {f,g}=f∘g−(−1)^{(p−1)(q−1)}g∘f; against DGAInfinity Layer 8 (arity zero, multiple brace): Θ(δx)=−[m,Θx] for x∈C⁰, Θ(f∘y)=Θf{Θy}, Θ{f,y}=[Θf,Θy] for y∈C⁰, and Θ(f∪g)=(−1)^{p(q−1)} m{Θf,Θg} for all p,q ≥ 0. Hence HH^n(A,A) = TauCeti.AInfinityAlgebra.PositiveHochschild.Cohomology 𝒜 (n−1) for n ≥ 2 with cohomologyBracket transported for p,q ≥ 2 (degree 0 of the pinned complex is Der_k(A), not HH¹), and HH^n(A,A) is Layer 8's Hochschild cohomology in Gerstenhaber degree n−1 for every n ≥ 0 with Layer 8's bracket transported to HH^•(A,A).
hypotheses: k a commutative ring
A a ring with Algebra k A
f ∈ C^p(A,A), g ∈ C^q(A,A)

api.name: HochschildHKR.suspendCochain_apply
api.statement: Θf(sa₁⊗…⊗sa_n)=s f(a₁,…,a_n) on degree-zero inputs; Θf is f on the length-n summand of TauCeti.ReducedTensorWords k A and 0 elsewhere.

api.name: HochschildHKR.bracket_one
api.statement: On C¹, {f,g}=f∘g−g∘f; on HH¹(A,A) the transported bracket is that of Der/Inn from TauCeti.derivationLieAlgebra; on the pinned complex it is the bracket of PositiveHochschild.Cohomology 𝒜 0 = Der_k(A) before the quotient by inner derivations.

api.name: HochschildHKR.suspendCochain_degree
api.statement: Layer 8's Hochschild cohomology of A sits in Gerstenhaber degrees ≥ −1, the degree −1 part being Z(A); the pinned positive-arity complex sees degrees ≥ 0, its degree-0 cohomology is Der_k(A) (no arity-zero cochains) and its degree-(n−1) cohomology is HH^n(A,A) for n ≥ 2.

tests.name: susp_n0
tests.statement: Arity zero (DGAInfinity Layer 8 only): for x∈C⁰, [m,Θx](sa)=s(xa−ax) while Θ(δx)(sa)=s(ax−xa): sign −1.

tests.name: susp_n1
tests.statement: At the pin (hochschildDifferential_eq_brace_sub, q=0): m{Θf}=s(f(a)b+af(b)), Θf{m}=sf(ab), so [m,Θf](sa⊗sb)=s(f(a)b+af(b)−f(ab))=Θ(δf)(sa⊗sb): sign +1; a uniform sign fails one of n=0, n=1.

tests.name: susp_n2
tests.statement: At the pin (q=1): m{Θf}(sa⊗sb⊗sc)=s(f(a,b)c−af(b,c)), Θf{m}=s(f(ab,c)−f(a,bc)), [m,Θf]=m{Θf}+Θf{m}=−Θ(δf): sign −1; the model m{F}−F{m} without (−1)^q gives s(a+ac−2ab) for f(a,b)=a on k[x] against δf=a−ac, equal to +Θ(δf) at (x,x,x) and −Θ(δf) at (x,1,x), so not ±Θ(δf) when 2≠0.

tests.name: susp_cup_10
tests.statement: Arity zero (Layer 8 only): for f∈C¹, y∈C⁰, m{Θf,Θy}(sa)=−s(f(a)y), so Θ(f∪y)=−m{Θf,Θy}; at (1,1) the sign is +1.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.cup_comm_homotopy
targets.statement: For f∈C^p(A,A), g∈C^q(A,A): g∪f − (−1)^{pq} f∪g = δf∘g + (−1)^q(δ(f∘g) − f∘δg); hence [g]∪[f]=(−1)^{pq}[f]∪[g] on HH^•(A,A).
hypotheses: k a commutative ring
A a ring with Algebra k A

locator.where: Proposition 6.6.4, line 1379 (the identity (6.6.3), line 1368, is used with corrected signs); Ger63 §7

tests.name: homotopy_11
tests.statement: At (1,1): f∘δg+δf∘g−δ(f∘g)=f∪g+g∪f; for f=g=∂ on k[x], 2(∂∪∂)=−δ(∂²), whereas Ginz05 (6.6.3) would give δ(∂²)=−2∂a∂b.

tests.name: homotopy_10_01_20
tests.statement: At (1,0), (0,1) and (2,0) both sides are a↦yf(a)−f(a)y, a↦xg(a)−g(a)x and (a,b)↦yf(a,b)−f(a,b)y.

tests.name: homotopy_leibniz
tests.statement: Adding (−1)^{pq} times the identity with f,g exchanged cancels the cup products and gives δ{f,g}={f,δg}−(−1)^q{δf,g} (using (−1)^{pq+p+q}=−(−1)^{(p−1)(q−1)}), which under 6.1 is the pinned Leibniz rule [m,[F,G]]=[[m,F],G]+(−1)^{|F|}[F,[m,G]] at |F|=p−1, |G|=q−1.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.chainComparison
targets.statement: There are signs ν_n∈{±1}, ν₀=1, such that a₀⊗a₁⊗…⊗a_n ↦ ν_n a₀⊗sa₁⊗…⊗sa_n is an isomorphism of complexes from C_•(A,A) (degree n in cohomological degree −n, via ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat) to the Hochschild chains of DGAInfinity Layer 8 of A in degree zero; for k-flat A, RefinedTraceMethods §1.1 identifies the homology of the cyclic bar complex with the derived HH_n(A/k) of KTheoryFiniteLocalFields §4.0, so HH_n(A,A) ≅ HH_n(A/k) naturally in A.

A a ring with Algebra k A

tests.name: chaincomp_k
tests.statement: For A=k both complexes have k in each degree with differentials alternating 0 and an isomorphism.

tests.name: chaincomp_Fp_Z
tests.statement: For k=ℤ, A=𝔽_p (not flat): classical HH₂=0 while derived HH₂(𝔽_p/ℤ)=𝔽_p (RefinedTraceMethods §§1.1, 1.10).

targets.name: HochschildHKR.antisymmetrization
targets.statement: For commutative R over k: the classical antisymmetrisation ε^cl_n: Ω^n_{R/k}→HH_n(R,R), r₀dr₁∧…∧dr_n ↦ [Σ_σ sgn(σ) r₀⊗r_{σ(1)}⊗…⊗r_{σ(n)}], is a well-defined natural R-linear map and, if R is flat over k, is carried by 6.3 to ν_n ε_n of RefinedTraceMethods §1.9; the classical projection π^cl_n:[r₀⊗…⊗r_n]↦r₀dr₁∧…∧dr_n is well defined and, if R is flat over k, corresponds to ν_n π_n; π^cl_n∘ε^cl_n=n!; ε^cl₁ is the inverse of 3.4; if R is smooth over k, ε^cl_n is an isomorphism for every n. The cycle and π∘b=0 computations hold for every commutative R; flatness enters only the comparison with the derived chains.

R a commutative ring with Algebra k R
Module.Flat k R for the comparison clauses with RefinedTraceMethods §1.9 in (a) and (b)
Algebra.Smooth k R for the last assertion (d)

api.name: HochschildHKR.antisymmetrization
api.statement: ε^cl_n as above, R-linear and natural in k→R.

api.name: HochschildHKR.projection
api.statement: π^cl_n as above, well defined on homology because π∘b=0.

api.name: HochschildHKR.projection_comp_antisymmetrization
api.statement: π^cl_n∘ε^cl_n = n!·id.

tests.name: antisym_kxy
tests.statement: For k[x,y], ε^cl₂(dx∧dy)=[1⊗x⊗y−1⊗y⊗x] and π^cl₂ε^cl₂(dx∧dy)=2dx∧dy; over 𝔽₂ the composite is 0 while ε^cl₂(dx∧dy)≠0.

tests.name: antisym_dual_numbers
tests.statement: For R=k[x]/(x²), flat not smooth, Ω²=0 while HH₂(R,R)≠0: ε^cl₂ not surjective.

tests.name: antisym_zero
tests.statement: ε^cl₀ is the identity of R=HH₀(R,R).

tests.name: antisym_Fp_Z

layers.title: Polyvector fields and the cohomological HKR theorem

targets.name: HochschildHKR.evalPairing
targets.statement: For commutative R and an R-module M (symmetric bimodule), f ↦ (r₀⊗r₁⊗…⊗r_n ↦ r₀ f(r₁,…,r_n)) is an isomorphism of cochain complexes of R-modules C^•(R,M) ≅ Hom_R(C_•(R,R),M) (ChainComplex.linearYonedaObj), natural in M; the evaluation pairing h_n: HH^n(R,M)→Hom_R(HH_n(R,R),M) is this isomorphism followed by the Kronecker map.
hypotheses: k a commutative ring
R a commutative ring with Algebra k R
M an R-module, viewed as a symmetric bimodule

api.name: HochschildHKR.evalPairing_apply
api.statement: h_n[f]([Σ r₀⊗r₁⊗…⊗r_n]) = Σ r₀ f(r₁,…,r_n).

api.name: HochschildHKR.evalPairing_one
api.statement: h₀ is the identity of M=Hom_R(R,M); under 3.3–3.4, h₁(D)(r₀dr₁)=r₀D(r₁), i.e. KaehlerDifferential.linearMapEquivDerivation.

api.name: HochschildHKR.evalPairing_natural
api.statement: h_n is R-linear and natural in M.

tests.name: eval_symmetric_needed

tests.name: eval_k
tests.statement: For R=k both sides vanish in positive degrees and h₀ is the identity.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.kronecker_bijective_of_projective_homology
targets.statement: For a chain complex X of projective R-modules indexed by ℕ and n with H_i(X) projective for all i<n, the Kronecker map H^i(Hom_R(X,M))→Hom_R(H_i(X),M) is bijective for every R-module M and every i≤n.
hypotheses: R a commutative ring
X : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ with every X_i projective
H_i(X) projective for i < n
i ≤ n

tests.name: kronecker_Z2

tests.name: kronecker_deg0
tests.statement: In degree 0 the map is always bijective: H⁰(Hom(X,M))=Hom(X₀/B₀,M).

tests.name: kronecker_acyclic
tests.statement: For R --id--> R both sides vanish.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.bijective_pairingDual_of_projective
targets.statement: For a finite projective R-module P and every n, ⋀[R]^n P is finite projective and exteriorPower.pairingDual R P n is bijective.

tests.statement: For P=0, ⋀⁰=R with identity pairing and ⋀^n=0 for n≥1.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.PolyvectorFields
targets.statement: T^n_{R/k} = ⋀[R]^n (Derivation k R R), T^• the exterior algebra of Der_k(R) over R; τ_n: T^n_{R/k}→Hom_R(Ω^n_{R/k},R), D₁∧…∧D_n ↦ (r₀dr₁∧…∧dr_n ↦ r₀det(D_j(r_i))), is pairingDual composed with ⋀^n of the inverse of KaehlerDifferential.linearMapEquivDerivation; τ_n is bijective when Ω¹ is finite projective, in particular for smooth R.

R a commutative ring with Algebra k R

api.name: HochschildHKR.polyvectorFields_zero_one
api.statement: T⁰ ≅ R and T¹ ≅ Der_k(R); the wedge product is graded commutative and strictly alternating.

api.name: HochschildHKR.polyvectorPairing

api.name: HochschildHKR.polyvectorPairing_bijective
api.statement: τ_n is bijective when Ω¹_{R/k} is finite projective, in particular when Algebra.Smooth k R.

api.name: HochschildHKR.homKaehler_eq_zero

tests.name: poly_inseparable
tests.statement: For K=𝔽₂(u), R=K[a]/(a²−u), Der_K(R)=R·∂ with ∂a=1 and T²=0.

targets.name: HochschildHKR.detCocycle
targets.statement: For D₁,…,D_n ∈ Der_k(R), ⟨D₁,…,D_n⟩ ∈ C^n(R,R), (r₁,…,r_n) ↦ det(D_j(r_i)); R-multilinear and alternating in the D_j (the unnormalised HKR map T^n→C^n(R,R)), a derivation in each r_i, a normalised cocycle, ⟨D⟩=D for n=1, ⟨⟩=1 for n=0, ⟨D₁,…,D_n⟩=Σ_σ sgn(σ) D_{σ(1)}∪…∪D_{σ(n)}, injective on cochains when Ω¹ is finite projective; Φ^n_HKR=(1/n!)⟨…⟩ when n! is invertible in k.

R a commutative ring with Algebra k R
n! invertible in k for Φ^n_HKR

api.name: HochschildHKR.hkrMap
api.statement: The unnormalised HKR map T^n_{R/k}→Z^n(R,R) induced by ⟨…⟩, and Φ^n_HKR=(1/n!)⟨…⟩ when n! is a unit.

api.name: HochschildHKR.detCocycle_eval
api.statement: For flat R, h_n[⟨D₁,…,D_n⟩](ε^cl_n(r₀dr₁∧…∧dr_n)) = n! r₀ det(D_j(r_i)) and h_n[D₁∪…∪D_n](ε^cl_n(…)) = r₀ det(D_j(r_i)).

api.name: HochschildHKR.detCocycle_mem_cocycles
api.statement: A cochain that is a derivation in each argument is a normalised Hochschild cocycle for commutative R.

api.name: HochschildHKR.detCocycle_class
api.statement: For every commutative R, [⟨D₁,…,D_n⟩] = n!·[D₁∪…∪D_n] in HH^n(R,R), by graded commutativity (6.2).

tests.name: det_kxy

gaps.title: The smooth HKR isomorphism is the antisymmetrisation map
gaps.detail: RefinedTraceMethods §1.9 names ε_n and proves π_n ε_n = n! and that ε₁ is an isomorphism; KTheoryFiniteLocalFields §4.0 asserts HH_n(A/k) ≅ Ω^n_{A/k} for smooth A without naming the map. The cohomological HKR theorem needs ε_n itself to be an isomorphism over every commutative base, which in characteristic p ≤ n does not follow from π_n ε_n = n!.
gaps.needs: A statement that ε_n : Ω^n_{A/k} → HH_n(A/k) is an isomorphism for every n, every commutative ring k and every smooth commutative k-algebra A, identified with the smooth HKR comparison of KTheoryFiniteLocalFields §4.0.
